app.name: Unhoard
app.tagline: See where your disk space went, and get it back safely.

top.growthHint: Colour the map by growth over the last week instead of by kind

map.keys: Cell map. Arrow keys move between cells, Enter zooms in, Backspace goes up, the Menu key opens the actions.
map.empty: Scan a drive to see where your space went.

details.unreadable: This folder could not be read without admin rights. Its size is unknown.
details.cloudState: {{local}} on this PC · {{cloud}} in the cloud

details.nothing: Select an item to see what it is.
details.largeReason: Large enough to be worth a look.
details.keepReason: Windows or a program needs this to work.

preview.title: Preview: nothing has changed yet
preview.notFreed: On the same drive this frees nothing yet: the space comes back after 30 days, or when you delete the items yourself.
preview.freeNote: Files become online-only. Nothing is deleted and nothing is downloaded.

reasons.changed: changed since the scan; scan again
reasons.insideSelection: already part of a selected folder

quarantine.title: Quarantine
quarantine.intro: Everything you move waits here for 30 days. Restore puts it back exactly where it was.
quarantine.restoredAs: Restored as {{name}}, because the original name is in use.

cloud.title: Cloud
cloud.none: No cloud folders were found on this PC.
cloud.scanFirst: Scan the drive that holds your cloud folder first.

photos.title: Photos & videos
photos.analyzing: Looking at your photos… nothing is downloaded.

certainty.likelyIdentical: Likely the same: same size, type and date or name

photos.keys: Arrows move · Space selects · Enter moves · N next group
photos.progress: Looking up thumbnails: {{done}} of {{total}}. Nothing is downloaded.
photos.start: Unhoard groups duplicates, bursts, chat media and screenshots by name, size and date. Photos that are only online stay online.
photos.cloudNote: These files are in the cloud. Unhoard does not move cloud files; remove a copy in OneDrive or Explorer.

settings.title: Settings
settings.privacy: Unhoard makes no network connections and sends nothing anywhere.
settings.license: Free software under the GNU GPL, version 3 or later.
settings.insightsText: Once a day, when the PC is idle, Unhoard measures the size of your largest folders, so History can show what grew. It stays on this PC, never reads file contents and uses at most 20 MB.
settings.chatText: Ask questions about your storage. A local AI model answers through Ollama on this PC; nothing goes to the internet. Lumen sees names and sizes from the scan, never file contents.

hints.language: The language of the whole app.
hints.mapStyle: How the overview draws your disk.
hints.adminRead: Read system folders with administrator rights.
hints.motion: Moving cells, or a still map.
hints.measure: Space really used, or the files' size.
hints.insights: Measures daily what grew, for History.
hints.chat: Ask questions; answered on this PC.

firstRun.title: Where did your space go?
firstRun.body: Unhoard maps your drive, explains every big item and helps you clear what you do not need. It never deletes anything without you, and everything you move can be restored for 30 days.
firstRun.privacy: Everything stays on this PC. No account, no network.

errors.staleScan: This view is out of date. Scan again.
errors.unknownItem: This item is no longer there. Scan again.
errors.invalidArgument: That did not work. Try again.
errors.busy: Wait until the scan has finished.

fs.locked: It is in use by another program. Close that program and try again.
fs.alreadyExists: Something with that name already exists.
fs.changed: It changed since the scan, so Unhoard left it alone. Scan again.

companion.name: Lumen
companion.drag: Drag to move, click for earlier messages

firstRun: Hi, I'm Lumen. I'll explain what you see, in bubbles like this one. Never in a popup.
scanStart: I'm scanning {{drive}} now. I only look; I change nothing.
scanProgress: {{files}} files counted. The big blocks are already showing.
scanDone: Done. The three largest: {{top}}. Click a cell to zoom in.
hiddenSpace: The striped cell is hidden space: {{size}} in use that the scan could not see, such as restore points. Click it to find out more.
revealDeclined: No problem. Without admin rights that part stays unknown, and nothing else changes.
revealDone: Revealed {{size}}. Most of it is usually restore points; manage those in System Protection.

safe: {{name}} is a cache: it is rebuilt by itself. Safe to move to the quarantine.
likelySafe: You probably no longer need {{name}}. From the quarantine you can restore it for 30 days.
review: Only you know whether you still need {{name}}. Have a look before you decide.
keep: {{name}} belongs to Windows or an app. Don't remove it by hand; the right Windows tool does it safely.
protected: {{name}} is a protected location. I explain it, but I never move it.

previewShown: First a preview, so you see exactly what will happen. Nothing has changed yet.
quarantineMoved: Moved to the quarantine. Note: not freed yet. I'll delete it after 30 days, and warn you first.

5: In 5 days I'll delete the batch from {{date}} ({{size}}). Restore anything you still want.
3: In 3 days I'll delete the batch from {{date}} ({{size}}).
1: Tomorrow I'll delete the batch from {{date}} ({{size}}). Last chance to restore.

deleteEarly: Want the space now? Open the folder, select the items and press Shift+Delete, or press Delete and empty the Recycle Bin.
restored: Put back exactly where it was.
freeUpSpaceDone: {{size}} is online-only now. It stays safe in the cloud.
photoReview: Each group starts with nothing selected. 'Select all but the keeper' keeps the best shot.
photoNoThumbs: Some cloud photos have no cached preview. I group those by name, size and date only, so nothing is downloaded.
windowsTool: I'm opening the Windows tool. That's the safe place to clean this up.
zoomTip: Backspace or the breadcrumb takes you back up.
cloudIntro: These files are also in the cloud. Free up space makes them online-only, without downloading or deleting anything.
adminAsk: Some folders cannot be read without admin rights, so their size stays unknown. May I read them? I only read, I change nothing.
adminReadDone: I read {{count}} protected folders with admin rights: {{size}} is no longer hidden.
growthFound: {{name}} grew by {{size}} recently. History shows what grew and when.

adobe-media-cache.explain: Preview files Premiere Pro and other Adobe apps made of your footage.
adobe-media-cache.reason: The app rebuilds it by itself. Close the app first.

amd-dxcache.title: AMD DirectX cache
amd-dxcache.explain: Shaders the AMD driver prepared for games.
amd-dxcache.reason: The app rebuilds it by itself. Close the app first.

android-emulators.title: Android emulators
android-emulators.explain: Virtual Android phones of Android Studio.
android-emulators.reason: It holds your data in one big file or folder.
android-emulators.action: Remove emulators you no longer use in the Device Manager of Android Studio.

android-sdk.title: Android SDK
android-sdk.explain: Android platforms, system images and tools.
android-sdk.reason: It holds your data in one big file or folder.

battlenet.explain: Games installed with Battle.net. Games often take tens of gigabytes each.

brave-cache.title: Brave cache
brave-cache.explain: Web pages and images Brave saved to load sites faster.
brave-cache.reason: The app rebuilds it by itself. Close the app first.

cargo-registry.title: Cargo registry
cargo-registry.explain: Packages Cargo downloaded once, kept to install them faster next time.
cargo-registry.reason: Cargo downloads them again when needed.

chrome-cache.title: Chrome cache
chrome-cache.explain: Web pages and images Chrome saved to load sites faster. Bookmarks and passwords are elsewhere.
chrome-cache.reason: The app rebuilds it by itself. Close the app first.

chrome-code-cache.title: Chrome code cache

chrome-code-cache.reason: The app rebuilds it by itself. Close the app first.

chrome-gpu-cache.title: Chrome graphics cache

chrome-gpu-cache.reason: The app rebuilds it by itself. Close the app first.

crash-dumps.title: App crash dumps
crash-dumps.explain: Crash reports that apps saved when they stopped unexpectedly.

d3d-shader-cache.title: DirectX shader cache
d3d-shader-cache.explain: Graphics shaders Windows prepared for games and apps.
d3d-shader-cache.reason: The app rebuilds it by itself. Close the app first.

delivery-optimization.title: Delivery Optimization files
delivery-optimization.explain: Update files Windows shares with other PCs to save bandwidth.
delivery-optimization.reason: Only a cache for sharing updates.
delivery-optimization.action: Clean it with Disk Cleanup › Delivery Optimization Files.

discord-cache.title: Discord cache
discord-cache.explain: Images and media Discord saved from your chats.
discord-cache.reason: The app rebuilds it by itself. Close the app first.

docker-disk.title: Docker Desktop disk
docker-disk.explain: Images, containers and volumes of Docker Desktop.
docker-disk.reason: It holds your data in one big file or folder.
docker-disk.action: Run docker system prune, then compact the disk in Docker Desktop.

dotnet-bin.title: .NET build output
dotnet-bin.explain: Build output of a .NET project (found next to its .csproj).
dotnet-bin.reason: It can be rebuilt with dotnet build.

dotnet-obj.title: .NET intermediate files
dotnet-obj.explain: Intermediate build files of a .NET project.
dotnet-obj.reason: It can be rebuilt with dotnet build.

downloads-extracted-zip.title: Already extracted archive
downloads-extracted-zip.explain: A ZIP file whose extracted folder is right next to it.
downloads-extracted-zip.reason: The content is already in the folder next to it.
downloads-extracted-zip.action: Move the ZIP to the quarantine.

downloads-iso.title: Disc images
downloads-iso.explain: ISO files: copies of installation discs or other disks.
downloads-iso.reason: Only you know whether you still need it.
downloads-iso.action: Check it, then move it to the quarantine.

downloads-old-installers.title: Old installers
downloads-old-installers.explain: Installers you downloaded more than a month ago. The programs are usually installed already, and you can download them again.
downloads-old-installers.reason: You can usually download them again.

driver-store.title: Driver store
driver-store.explain: Every driver Windows has installed, so it can reinstall them.
driver-store.reason: Windows needs it for your hardware.

ea-games.title: EA games
ea-games.explain: Games installed with the EA app. Games often take tens of gigabytes each.
ea-games.reason: Only you know which games you still play.
ea-games.action: Uninstall games through the EA app, so it stays consistent. Unhoard never moves a game folder.

edge-cache.title: Edge cache
edge-cache.explain: Web pages and images Edge saved to load sites faster. Favourites and passwords are elsewhere.
edge-cache.reason: The app rebuilds it by itself. Close the app first.

edge-code-cache.title: Edge code cache
edge-code-cache.explain: Compiled website scripts Edge keeps to start sites faster.
edge-code-cache.reason: The app rebuilds it by itself. Close the app first.

epic-games.title: Epic Games
epic-games.explain: Games installed with the Epic Games Launcher. Games often take tens of gigabytes each.
epic-games.reason: Only you know which games you still play.
epic-games.action: Uninstall games through the Epic Games Launcher, so it stays consistent. Unhoard never moves a game folder.

firefox-cache.title: Firefox cache
firefox-cache.explain: Web pages and images Firefox saved to load sites faster. Bookmarks and passwords are elsewhere.
firefox-cache.reason: The app rebuilds it by itself. Close the app first.

gradle-caches.title: Gradle caches
gradle-caches.explain: Packages Gradle downloaded once, kept to install them faster next time.
gradle-caches.reason: Gradle downloads them again when needed.

hiberfil.title: Hibernation file
hiberfil.explain: Windows writes your memory here for hibernate and Fast Startup. Its size follows your RAM.
hiberfil.reason: Windows needs it while hibernation is on.
hiberfil.action: To make it smaller, run powercfg /h /type reduced as administrator. That also affects Fast Startup.

huggingface-cache.title: Hugging Face models
huggingface-cache.explain: AI models downloaded by Hugging Face tools.
huggingface-cache.reason: It holds your data in one big file or folder.

hyperv-disks.title: Hyper-V virtual disk
hyperv-disks.explain: The disk of a Hyper-V virtual machine.
hyperv-disks.reason: It holds your data in one big file or folder.
hyperv-disks.action: Remove machines you no longer need in Hyper-V Manager.

maven-repository.title: Maven repository
maven-repository.explain: Packages Maven downloaded once, kept to install them faster next time.
maven-repository.reason: Maven downloads them again when needed.

memory-dump.title: Crash memory dump
memory-dump.explain: A full copy of memory from the last system crash, for troubleshooting.
memory-dump.reason: Only useful to analyse that crash.
memory-dump.action: Remove it with Disk Cleanup › System error memory dump files.

minidump.title: Crash minidumps
minidump.explain: Small crash reports from earlier system crashes.
minidump.reason: Only useful to analyse those crashes.

node-modules.title: node_modules
node-modules.explain: The installed packages of a JavaScript project (found next to its package.json).
node-modules.reason: It can be rebuilt with npm install.

npm-cache.title: npm cache
npm-cache.explain: Packages npm downloaded once, kept to install them faster next time.
npm-cache.reason: npm downloads them again when needed.

nuget-http-cache.title: NuGet HTTP cache
nuget-http-cache.explain: Packages NuGet downloaded once, kept to install them faster next time.
nuget-http-cache.reason: NuGet downloads them again when needed.

nuget-packages.title: NuGet packages
nuget-packages.explain: Packages NuGet downloaded once, kept to install them faster next time.
nuget-packages.reason: NuGet downloads them again when needed.

nvidia-dxcache.title: NVIDIA DirectX cache
nvidia-dxcache.explain: Shaders the NVIDIA driver prepared for DirectX games.
nvidia-dxcache.reason: The app rebuilds it by itself. Close the app first.

nvidia-glcache.title: NVIDIA OpenGL cache
nvidia-glcache.explain: Shaders the NVIDIA driver prepared for OpenGL apps.
nvidia-glcache.reason: The app rebuilds it by itself. Close the app first.

ollama-models.title: Ollama models
ollama-models.reason: It holds your data in one big file or folder.

package-cache.title: Installer package cache
package-cache.explain: Installers that programs need to repair or uninstall themselves.
package-cache.reason: Without it programs cannot be repaired or removed.

pagefile.title: Page file
pagefile.explain: Virtual memory: Windows uses it when RAM runs low and for crash dumps.
pagefile.reason: Windows needs it, also with plenty of RAM.
pagefile.action: Leave it alone. Never turn the page file off.

phone-backup-apple-devices.title: iPhone backup (Apple Devices)
phone-backup-apple-devices.explain: A full backup of an iPhone or iPad made by the Apple Devices app.
phone-backup-apple-devices.reason: Only you know whether you have a newer backup.
phone-backup-apple-devices.action: Check you have a newer backup, then move it to the quarantine.

phone-backup-itunes.title: iPhone backup (iTunes)
phone-backup-itunes.explain: A full backup of an iPhone or iPad made by iTunes.
phone-backup-itunes.reason: Only you know whether you have a newer backup.
phone-backup-itunes.action: Check you have a newer backup, then move it to the quarantine.

pip-cache.title: pip cache
pip-cache.explain: Packages pip downloaded once, kept to install them faster next time.
pip-cache.reason: pip downloads them again when needed.

pnpm-store.title: pnpm store
pnpm-store.explain: Packages pnpm downloaded once, kept to install them faster next time.
pnpm-store.reason: pnpm downloads them again when needed.

python-venv.title: Python virtual environment
python-venv.explain: The installed packages of a Python project.
python-venv.reason: It can be rebuilt with pip install -r requirements.txt.

recycle-bin.title: Recycle Bin
recycle-bin.explain: Files you already deleted. They take space until the Recycle Bin is emptied.
recycle-bin.reason: You already chose to delete them.
recycle-bin.action: Check it, then empty the Recycle Bin.

rust-target.title: Rust build folder
rust-target.explain: Build output of a Rust project (found next to its Cargo.toml).
rust-target.reason: It can be rebuilt with cargo build.

steam-games.title: Steam games
steam-games.explain: Games installed with Steam. Games often take tens of gigabytes each.
steam-games.reason: Only you know which games you still play.
steam-games.action: Uninstall games through Steam, so it stays consistent. Unhoard never moves a game folder.

steam-shadercache.title: Steam shader cache
steam-shadercache.explain: Shaders Steam prepared for your games. Steam rebuilds them when you play.
steam-shadercache.reason: The app rebuilds it by itself. Close the app first.

swapfile.title: Swap file
swapfile.explain: A small helper file Windows uses for apps from the Store.

system-volume-information.title: Restore points
system-volume-information.explain: Restore points and shadow copies that let Windows undo system changes.
system-volume-information.reason: Deleting them blindly removes your safety net.
system-volume-information.action: Manage them in System Protection: choose how much space they may use, or delete old ones.

thumbnail-cache.title: Thumbnail cache
thumbnail-cache.explain: Small previews Explorer made of your pictures and videos.
thumbnail-cache.reason: Explorer makes them again when needed.
thumbnail-cache.action: Clean it with Disk Cleanup › Thumbnails.

ubisoft-games.title: Ubisoft games
ubisoft-games.explain: Games installed with Ubisoft Connect. Games often take tens of gigabytes each.
ubisoft-games.reason: Only you know which games you still play.
ubisoft-games.action: Uninstall games through Ubisoft Connect, so it stays consistent. Unhoard never moves a game folder.

update-downloads.title: Windows Update downloads
update-downloads.explain: Update files Windows already installed or still has to install.
update-downloads.reason: Windows downloads them again when needed.
update-downloads.action: Clean it with Disk Cleanup › Clean up system files › Windows Update Cleanup.

user-temp.title: Your temporary files
user-temp.explain: Apps leave temporary files here and often forget to clean them up.
user-temp.reason: It is at least a day old; apps recreate what they need, and items still in use are skipped.

virtualbox-vms.title: VirtualBox machine
virtualbox-vms.explain: A VirtualBox virtual machine with its disks.
virtualbox-vms.reason: It holds your data in one big file or folder.
virtualbox-vms.action: Remove machines you no longer need in VirtualBox.

vmware-vms.title: VMware machine
vmware-vms.explain: A VMware virtual machine with its disks.
vmware-vms.reason: It holds your data in one big file or folder.
vmware-vms.action: Remove machines you no longer need in VMware.

windows-installer.title: Windows Installer cache
windows-installer.explain: Copies of installers Windows needs to repair, update or remove your programs.
windows-installer.reason: Without it programs cannot be repaired or removed.
windows-installer.action: Leave it alone. Remove programs you no longer use in Settings › Apps.

windows-old.title: Previous Windows installation
windows-old.explain: A copy of your previous Windows, kept after an upgrade so you can go back. Windows removes it after about 10 days, or you can remove it yourself.
windows-old.reason: Only needed to roll back an upgrade.
windows-old.action: Remove it with Disk Cleanup › Previous Windows installation(s).

windows-temp.title: Windows temporary files
windows-temp.explain: Temporary files of Windows and installers.
windows-temp.action: Clean it with Disk Cleanup › Clean up system files.

winsxs.title: Windows component store
winsxs.explain: Holds the Windows components and updates. Explorer shows it larger than it is, because many files are hard links shared with System32.
winsxs.reason: Removing files by hand breaks Windows Update and repairs.
winsxs.action: Disk Cleanup cleans old components safely, or run DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /StartComponentCleanup.

wsl-disk.title: WSL Linux disk
wsl-disk.explain: The virtual disk of a Linux distribution in WSL. It grows as you use it, but never shrinks by itself.
wsl-disk.reason: It holds your data in one big file or folder.
wsl-disk.action: Clean up inside Linux, then compact the disk (wsl --manage <distro> --set-sparse true, or Optimize-VHD).

wsl-disk-store.title: WSL Linux disk
wsl-disk-store.explain: The virtual disk of a Linux distribution in WSL. It grows as you use it, but never shrinks by itself.
wsl-disk-store.reason: It holds your data in one big file or folder.
wsl-disk-store.action: Clean up inside Linux, then compact the disk.

xbox-games.title: Xbox games
xbox-games.explain: Games installed with the Xbox app. Games often take tens of gigabytes each.
xbox-games.reason: Only you know which games you still play.
xbox-games.action: Uninstall games through the Xbox app, so it stays consistent. Unhoard never moves a game folder.

yarn-cache.title: Yarn cache
yarn-cache.explain: Packages Yarn downloaded once, kept to install them faster next time.
yarn-cache.reason: Yarn downloads them again when needed.

conda-pkgs-miniconda.title: conda package cache
conda-pkgs-miniconda.explain: Packages conda downloaded and unpacked to build your environments.
conda-pkgs-miniconda.reason: Your environments keep working; conda downloads packages again when it needs them.
conda-pkgs-miniconda.action: Run conda clean --all in the Anaconda Prompt.

conda-pkgs-anaconda.title: conda package cache
conda-pkgs-anaconda.explain: Packages conda downloaded and unpacked to build your environments.
conda-pkgs-anaconda.reason: Your environments keep working; conda downloads packages again when it needs them.
conda-pkgs-anaconda.action: Run conda clean --all in the Anaconda Prompt.

go-mod-cache.title: Go module cache
go-mod-cache.explain: Source code of Go modules, downloaded once for your projects.
go-mod-cache.reason: Go downloads modules again when a build needs them.

bun-cache.title: Bun cache
bun-cache.explain: Packages Bun downloaded once, kept to install them faster.
bun-cache.reason: Bun downloads them again when needed.

uv-cache.title: uv cache
uv-cache.explain: Python packages uv downloaded and built, shared by your projects.
uv-cache.reason: uv downloads or builds them again when needed.

poetry-cache.title: Poetry cache
poetry-cache.reason: Poetry downloads them again when needed.

whisper-models.title: Whisper speech models
whisper-models.explain: Speech-recognition models that Whisper downloaded the first time you used them.
whisper-models.reason: Whisper downloads a model again the next time you use it, which can take a while.
whisper-models.action: Move it to the quarantine if you no longer transcribe audio.

torch-hub.title: PyTorch Hub models
torch-hub.explain: Models and code PyTorch Hub downloaded for scripts you ran.
torch-hub.reason: PyTorch downloads them again when a script needs them.

ollama-updates.title: Ollama update downloads
ollama-updates.explain: Installers Ollama downloaded to update itself.
ollama-updates.reason: Ollama downloads a new one for its next update.

vscode-caches.title: VS Code caches
vscode-caches.explain: Caches Visual Studio Code builds up: old versions, extension downloads and web content.
vscode-caches.reason: VS Code rebuilds them; close it first, or the files are in use.
vscode-caches.action: Close VS Code, then move it to the quarantine.

cursor-caches.title: Cursor caches
cursor-caches.explain: Caches the Cursor editor builds up: old versions, extension downloads and web content.
cursor-caches.reason: Cursor rebuilds them; close it first, or the files are in use.
cursor-caches.action: Close Cursor, then move it to the quarantine.

teams-cache.title: Microsoft Teams cache
teams-cache.explain: Cached chats, images and web content of the new Microsoft Teams.
teams-cache.reason: Microsoft documents clearing it; Teams downloads what it needs again. Quit Teams first.
teams-cache.action: Quit Teams, then move it to the quarantine.

slack-cache.title: Slack cache
slack-cache.explain: Images, files and web content Slack keeps to load faster.
slack-cache.reason: Slack rebuilds it; quit Slack first.
slack-cache.action: Quit Slack, then move it to the quarantine.

epic-webcache.title: Epic Games Launcher web cache
epic-webcache.explain: Web pages and images of the Epic Games Launcher.
epic-webcache.reason: The launcher rebuilds it; Epic's support suggests clearing it when the launcher misbehaves.
epic-webcache.action: Quit the launcher, then move it to the quarantine.

steam-htmlcache.title: Steam web cache
steam-htmlcache.explain: Pages and images of Steam's built-in browser (the store and the community).
steam-htmlcache.reason: Steam rebuilds it; quit Steam first.
steam-htmlcache.action: Quit Steam, then move it to the quarantine.

outlook-offline-mail.title: Outlook offline mailbox
outlook-offline-mail.explain: A copy of your mailbox that Outlook keeps on this PC (an .ost file), so mail works offline.
outlook-offline-mail.reason: The mail itself stays on the server, but Outlook downloads everything again if the file is gone.
outlook-offline-mail.action: In Outlook, keep less mail offline: Account settings › your account › Change › Mail to keep offline.

lmstudio-models.title: LM Studio models
lmstudio-models.explain: Language models you downloaded in LM Studio.
lmstudio-models.reason: Only you know which models you still use; downloading one again takes a while.
lmstudio-models.action: Delete models you no longer use in LM Studio, under My Models.

lmstudio-models-cache.title: LM Studio models
lmstudio-models-cache.explain: Language models you downloaded in LM Studio.
lmstudio-models-cache.reason: Only you know which models you still use; downloading one again takes a while.
lmstudio-models-cache.action: Delete models you no longer use in LM Studio, under My Models.

jetbrains-caches.title: JetBrains IDE caches
jetbrains-caches.explain: Indexes and caches of a JetBrains IDE such as IntelliJ IDEA or PyCharm.
jetbrains-caches.reason: The IDE rebuilds them, which takes a while the first time; close the IDE first.
jetbrains-caches.action: Close the IDE, then move it to the quarantine.

unity-cache.title: Unity cache
unity-cache.explain: Downloaded packages and assets the Unity editor shares between projects.
unity-cache.reason: Unity downloads them again when a project needs them.

rustup-toolchains.title: Rust toolchains
rustup-toolchains.explain: Rust compilers rustup installed, one folder per version.
rustup-toolchains.reason: Only you know which versions your projects need.
rustup-toolchains.action: List them with rustup toolchain list and remove old ones with rustup toolchain uninstall <name>.

wsl-rdclient-traces.title: WSL Remote Desktop traces
wsl-rdclient-traces.explain: Diagnostic traces of the Remote Desktop client WSL uses to show Linux apps in a window (WSLg). A known issue can make them grow by tens of gigabytes a day.
wsl-rdclient-traces.reason: They are only logs; nothing needs them.
wsl-rdclient-traces.action: Quit Docker Desktop and run wsl --shutdown, then move it to the quarantine. If you never use Linux apps with a window, add guiApplications=false under [wsl2] in .wslconfig in your profile folder.

def-windows.title: Windows itself
def-windows.explain: The operating system: its programs, drivers and built-in apps. Unhoard never touches it; Disk Cleanup can shrink it safely.

def-program-files.title: Installed programs (64-bit)
def-program-files.explain: Programs installed for everyone on this PC. Remove a program through Settings › Apps, never by deleting its folder here.

def-program-files-x86.title: Installed programs (32-bit)
def-program-files-x86.explain: Older 32-bit programs, installed for everyone on this PC. Remove a program through Settings › Apps.

def-programdata.title: Shared program data
def-programdata.explain: Data that programs share between all users: licences, databases, caches and downloaded updates. Windows hides this folder by default.

def-users.title: Everyone's personal folders
def-users.explain: One folder per person who uses this PC, with their documents, desktop, downloads and app settings.

def-perflogs.title: Performance logs
def-perflogs.explain: Where Windows stores performance measurements when someone asks for them. It is usually empty.

def-recovery.title: Windows recovery environment
def-recovery.explain: The repair tools Windows starts when the PC no longer boots. Small, and needed in an emergency.

def-winreagent.title: Recovery update files
def-winreagent.explain: Working files Windows uses to update its recovery environment during an update. Windows clears it by itself.

def-windows-bt.title: Windows upgrade files
def-windows-bt.explain: Installation files of a Windows upgrade. Disk Cleanup removes them under “Temporary Windows installation files”.

def-windows-ws.title: Windows setup download
def-windows-ws.explain: Files the Windows setup or Media Creation Tool downloaded to install or upgrade Windows. Disk Cleanup removes them.

def-getcurrent.title: Update Assistant leftovers
def-getcurrent.explain: Logs and setup files left by the Windows Update Assistant after a feature update.

def-sysreset.title: PC reset logs
def-sysreset.explain: Logs of a “Reset this PC” attempt. Useful only when a reset failed.

def-msocache.title: Office installation cache
def-msocache.explain: A local copy of the Office installation files that older Office versions keep for repairs.

def-config-msi.title: Installer rollback files
def-config-msi.explain: Files the Windows Installer keeps so it can undo an install that fails halfway.

def-root-intel.title: Unpacked Intel drivers
def-root-intel.explain: Driver installers from Intel, unpacked here during installation. The drivers themselves are already installed elsewhere.

def-root-amd.title: Unpacked AMD drivers
def-root-amd.explain: Driver installers from AMD, unpacked here during installation. The drivers themselves are already installed elsewhere.

def-root-nvidia.title: Unpacked NVIDIA drivers
def-root-nvidia.explain: Driver installers from NVIDIA, unpacked here during installation. The drivers themselves are already installed elsewhere.

def-swsetup.title: HP software installers
def-swsetup.explain: Copies of the installers for the software and drivers HP put on this PC.

def-onedrivetemp.title: OneDrive working files
def-onedrivetemp.explain: Temporary files OneDrive uses while it syncs. OneDrive clears them itself.

def-inetpub.title: Web server folder
def-inetpub.explain: The folder of Windows' built-in web server (IIS): websites hosted on this PC and their logs.

def-msys64.title: MSYS2
def-msys64.explain: A Unix-like toolset for Windows developers, with its own installed packages.

def-esd.title: Windows installation download
def-esd.explain: Windows installation files downloaded by the Media Creation Tool. Not needed once the upgrade or USB stick is done.

def-dumpstack.title: Crash log
def-dumpstack.explain: A small log Windows writes while it handles a crash.

def-bootmgr.title: Windows boot manager
def-bootmgr.explain: The program that starts Windows when the PC is switched on.

def-system32.title: The core of Windows
def-system32.explain: System programs, libraries and drivers (64-bit). Almost everything in Windows depends on it.

def-syswow64.title: 32-bit system files
def-syswow64.explain: The 32-bit counterpart of System32, so older 32-bit programs keep working.

def-softwaredistribution.title: Windows Update's working folder
def-softwaredistribution.explain: Downloaded updates and the update history. The downloads inside can be cleared; the folder itself stays.

def-fonts.title: Installed fonts
def-fonts.explain: Every font installed for all users of this PC.

def-win-logs.title: Windows component logs
def-win-logs.explain: Logs of Windows components such as updates (CBS) and repairs (DISM). Disk Cleanup trims them.

def-prefetch.title: Startup hints
def-prefetch.explain: Small files that record how programs start, so Windows can launch them faster. Windows manages its size.

def-assembly.title: .NET shared libraries
def-assembly.explain: Libraries that .NET Framework programs share (the global assembly cache), plus their precompiled versions.

def-microsoft-net.title: .NET Framework
def-microsoft-net.explain: The .NET Framework itself: the runtime many Windows programs need.

def-servicing.title: Update servicing
def-servicing.explain: The tools and packages Windows uses to install updates and switch features on or off.

def-systemapps.title: Built-in Windows apps
def-systemapps.explain: Apps that are part of Windows itself, such as Start, Search and the lock screen.

def-systemresources.title: System resources
def-systemresources.explain: Images, icons and text that Windows' own programs show.

def-panther.title: Windows Setup logs
def-panther.explain: Logs of installing and upgrading Windows. Useful only when an upgrade went wrong.

def-livekernelreports.title: Driver problem dumps
def-livekernelreports.explain: Memory dumps of driver or hardware problems that did not crash the PC. They can grow to gigabytes; Disk Cleanup removes them under “System error memory dump files”.

def-inf.title: Driver setup information
def-inf.explain: The setup information of installed drivers and Windows components.

def-globalization.title: Language and region data
def-globalization.explain: Sorting rules, time zones and other data Windows needs for languages and regions.

def-ime.title: Input method editors
def-ime.explain: The tools for typing languages such as Chinese, Japanese and Korean.

def-win-boot.title: Boot files
def-win-boot.explain: The files Windows copies to the boot partition so the PC can start.

def-win-media.title: Windows sounds
def-win-media.explain: The sounds Windows plays for notifications, errors and start-up.

def-win-web.title: Wallpapers
def-win-web.explain: The desktop backgrounds and lock screen pictures that come with Windows.

def-cursors.title: Mouse pointers
def-cursors.explain: The mouse pointer shapes that come with Windows.

def-speech.title: Speech recognition
def-speech.explain: The speech recognition engine and voices of classic Windows.

def-speech-onecore.title: Voices and dictation
def-speech-onecore.explain: The voices and dictation models Windows uses for Narrator and voice typing.

def-shellexperiences.title: Windows shell parts
def-shellexperiences.explain: Parts of the Windows interface, such as the notification centre and quick settings.

def-appcompat.title: Compatibility data
def-appcompat.explain: What Windows knows about making older programs work, plus its record of installed programs.

def-apppatch.title: Compatibility fixes
def-apppatch.explain: Fixes Windows applies to specific older programs so they run correctly.

def-win-debug.title: Debug logs
def-win-debug.explain: Logs a few Windows services write for troubleshooting.

def-serviceprofiles.title: Profiles of system services
def-serviceprofiles.explain: The personal folders of the built-in service accounts (Local Service and Network Service), including their caches.

def-systemtemp.title: Temporary files of system services
def-systemtemp.explain: Temporary files written by services that run as the system, such as browser updaters.

def-win-security.title: Security policy data
def-win-security.explain: The databases and logs of Windows' local security policy.

def-policydefinitions.title: Group policy templates
def-policydefinitions.explain: The templates that describe every group policy setting.

def-rescache.title: Resource cache
def-rescache.explain: A cache of text and images that speeds up Windows' own apps.

def-csc.title: Offline files cache
def-csc.explain: Local copies of network files marked “always available offline”.

def-downloaded-program-files.title: Old browser add-ons
def-downloaded-program-files.explain: ActiveX controls that Internet Explorer downloaded. Disk Cleanup can empty it.

def-win-resources.title: Themes
def-win-resources.explain: The themes and visual styles of Windows.

def-win-tasks.title: Scheduled tasks (old format)
def-win-tasks.explain: Scheduled tasks stored in the format of older Windows versions.

def-containers.title: Windows container images
def-containers.explain: Base files for Windows Sandbox and Windows containers.

def-uus.title: Update stack
def-uus.explain: The part of Windows Update that installs the updates, kept separately so it can update itself.

def-win-help.title: Help files
def-win-help.explain: Help files of Windows and some older programs.

def-win-provisioning.title: Provisioning packages
def-win-provisioning.explain: Settings packages used to set up a PC for a school or company.

def-win-migration.title: Upgrade migration rules
def-win-migration.explain: The rules Windows follows to carry settings over during an upgrade.

def-win-system.title: 16-bit leftovers
def-win-system.explain: A few files kept so that very old 16-bit programs still find what they expect.

def-s32-drivers.title: Device drivers
def-s32-drivers.explain: The drivers Windows loads for your hardware.

def-s32-config.title: The registry
def-s32-config.explain: The Windows registry: the settings of Windows, hardware, programs and user accounts.

def-s32-winevt.title: Event logs
def-s32-winevt.explain: The logs you see in Event Viewer. Windows caps their size.

def-s32-spool.title: Print queue
def-s32-spool.explain: Print jobs waiting for the printer, plus printer drivers.

def-s32-catroot2.title: Update signature database
def-s32-catroot2.explain: The signatures Windows uses to check that updates and drivers are genuine.

def-s32-logfiles.title: System log files
def-s32-logfiles.explain: Logs of Windows services such as the firewall, Wi-Fi and setup. Windows rotates most of them.

def-s32-tasks.title: Scheduled tasks
def-s32-tasks.explain: Every task in Task Scheduler, from Windows and from your programs.

def-s32-sru.title: Resource usage history
def-s32-sru.explain: The database behind Task Manager's app history and the data usage overview.

def-s32-wdi.title: Diagnostic traces
def-s32-wdi.explain: Traces Windows records to diagnose slow start-up and shutdown.

def-s32-wbem.title: Management database (WMI)
def-s32-wbem.explain: The database and tools programs use to ask Windows about hardware and settings.

def-sd-datastore.title: Update history database
def-sd-datastore.explain: The database in which Windows Update keeps which updates are installed.

def-desktop.title: Your desktop
def-desktop.explain: Everything you see on your desktop: files, folders and shortcuts.

def-documents.title: Your documents
def-documents.explain: The standard place for your own documents. Many programs and games also keep their saves and settings here.

def-pictures.title: Your pictures
def-pictures.explain: The standard place for your photos, screenshots and other images.

def-videos.title: Your videos
def-videos.explain: The standard place for your videos, including screen and game recordings.

def-music.title: Your music
def-music.explain: The standard place for your music and other sound files.

def-downloads.title: Your downloads
def-downloads.explain: Everything your browsers and apps downloaded. It fills up unnoticed: installers, archives and files you opened once.

def-favorites.title: Favourites
def-favorites.explain: The favourites of Internet Explorer and some older programs.

def-links.title: Quick access links
def-links.explain: Shortcuts that older Windows versions showed in Explorer's sidebar.

def-contacts.title: Contacts
def-contacts.explain: Address cards of the old Windows Contacts feature. Usually empty.

def-saved-games.title: Saved games
def-saved-games.explain: Where some games keep your progress and settings.

def-3d-objects.title: 3D objects
def-3d-objects.explain: The standard place for 3D models, made for the Paint 3D app. Usually empty.

def-onedrive.title: Your OneDrive folder
def-onedrive.explain: The files OneDrive keeps in sync with the cloud. A file marked online-only takes no space here; “Free up space” turns local copies back into online-only ones.

def-appdata.title: App data
def-appdata.explain: Where your programs keep their own data for your account: settings, caches, logs and sometimes downloads. Windows hides it by default.

def-ntuser-dat.title: Your part of the registry
def-ntuser-dat.explain: Your personal Windows settings: the part of the registry that belongs to your account.

def-dropbox.title: Your Dropbox folder
def-dropbox.explain: The files Dropbox keeps in sync with the cloud.

def-icloud-drive.title: Your iCloud Drive folder
def-icloud-drive.explain: The files iCloud keeps in sync with Apple's cloud.

def-creative-cloud-files.title: Creative Cloud files
def-creative-cloud-files.explain: The files Adobe Creative Cloud keeps in sync with your Adobe account.

def-source.title: Your code projects
def-source.explain: Where Visual Studio creates new projects (in “repos”). It holds your own source code and build output.

def-scoop.title: Scoop
def-scoop.explain: Programs installed with the Scoop package manager, with every installed version and its download cache.

def-go-workspace.title: Go workspace
def-go-workspace.explain: The workspace of the Go language: downloaded modules and tools you built.

def-miniconda.title: Miniconda
def-miniconda.explain: A Python distribution with its environments and downloaded packages.

def-anaconda.title: Anaconda
def-anaconda.explain: A large Python distribution for data science, with its environments and downloaded packages.

def-intel-graphics-profiles.title: Intel graphics profiles
def-intel-graphics-profiles.explain: Display profiles saved by Intel's graphics software. Tiny.

def-dot-ssh.title: SSH keys
def-dot-ssh.explain: Your SSH keys and the list of servers you trust. Losing them locks you out of servers and Git hosts.

def-dot-gitconfig.title: Git settings
def-dot-gitconfig.explain: Your Git name, e-mail address and preferences.

def-dot-docker.title: Docker settings
def-dot-docker.explain: Docker's settings and sign-in for your account. The images and containers live in Docker's virtual disk, not here.

def-dot-vscode.title: VS Code extensions
def-dot-vscode.explain: The extensions you installed in Visual Studio Code. Remove one from within VS Code.

def-dot-cursor.title: Cursor extensions
def-dot-cursor.explain: The extensions and settings of the Cursor code editor.

def-dot-claude.title: Claude Code data
def-dot-claude.explain: Settings, memory and conversation history of Claude Code.

def-dot-cache.title: Tool caches
def-dot-cache.explain: A shared cache folder for developer and AI tools: downloaded models, packages and build results. Each tool refills what it needs.

def-dot-config.title: Tool settings
def-dot-config.explain: Settings of command-line tools that follow the Linux convention.

def-dot-nuget.title: NuGet
def-dot-nuget.explain: The .NET package manager's folder; the downloaded packages inside can be cleared and come back on the next build.

def-dot-cargo.title: Cargo (Rust)
def-dot-cargo.explain: Rust's package manager: the tools you installed with it and the packages it downloaded.

def-dot-rustup.title: Rust toolchains
def-dot-rustup.explain: The Rust compilers rustup installed, one folder per version.

def-dot-gradle.title: Gradle
def-dot-gradle.explain: The Gradle build tool: downloaded Gradle versions and the libraries your Java and Android projects use.

def-dot-m2.title: Maven
def-dot-m2.explain: The Maven build tool's folder with downloaded Java libraries.

def-dot-android.title: Android tools data
def-dot-android.explain: Settings of the Android development tools and the virtual phones of the emulator.

def-dot-conda.title: Conda environments
def-dot-conda.explain: Python environments and package caches that conda created in your profile.

def-dot-ollama.title: Ollama
def-dot-ollama.explain: Ollama's folder: the AI models you downloaded and its keys. Remove a model with Ollama, so its list stays right.

def-dot-lmstudio.title: LM Studio
def-dot-lmstudio.explain: LM Studio's folder: downloaded AI models, chats and settings.

def-dot-aws.title: AWS credentials
def-dot-aws.explain: Your access keys and settings for Amazon Web Services.

def-dot-azure.title: Azure CLI data
def-dot-azure.explain: Sign-in tokens, settings and logs of the Azure command-line tool.

def-dot-kube.title: Kubernetes settings
def-dot-kube.explain: The clusters kubectl can reach, plus its cache.

def-dot-dotnet.title: .NET tools
def-dot-dotnet.explain: Tools you installed with “dotnet tool” and data of the .NET command line.

def-dot-templateengine.title: .NET project templates
def-dot-templateengine.explain: The cache of project templates for “dotnet new”.

def-dot-ipython.title: IPython settings
def-dot-ipython.explain: Settings and command history of the interactive Python shell.

def-dot-keras.title: Keras data
def-dot-keras.explain: Datasets and pretrained models that Keras downloaded.

def-dot-bun.title: Bun
def-dot-bun.explain: The Bun JavaScript runtime and its package cache.

def-dot-deno.title: Deno
def-dot-deno.explain: The Deno JavaScript runtime and the tools installed with it.

def-dot-pyenv.title: pyenv Python versions
def-dot-pyenv.explain: The Python versions pyenv installed, one folder per version.

def-dot-vs.title: Visual Studio workspace cache
def-dot-vs.explain: Visual Studio's cache for folders you opened without a project.

def-dot-wslconfig.title: WSL settings
def-dot-wslconfig.explain: Your settings for the Windows Subsystem for Linux, such as its memory limit.

def-docs-my-games.title: Game saves and settings
def-docs-my-games.explain: Where many games keep your saved games, settings and screenshots. Deleting a game's folder here loses its progress unless the game syncs to the cloud.

def-docs-office-templates.title: Your Office templates
def-docs-office-templates.explain: Templates you saved yourself in Word, Excel or PowerPoint.

def-docs-outlook-files.title: Outlook data files
def-docs-outlook-files.explain: Mailboxes and archives of classic Outlook (.pst). An archive here can be the only copy of old mail.

def-docs-powershell.title: PowerShell profile and modules
def-docs-powershell.explain: Your PowerShell start-up script and the modules you installed for your account.

def-docs-visual-studio.title: Visual Studio user files
def-docs-visual-studio.explain: Your Visual Studio templates, code snippets and settings.

def-docs-zoom.title: Zoom recordings
def-docs-zoom.explain: Meetings you recorded with Zoom on this PC, one folder per meeting.

def-docs-onenote.title: OneNote notebooks
def-docs-onenote.explain: Notebooks of the desktop version of OneNote that are stored on this PC.

def-docs-sound-recordings.title: Sound recordings
def-docs-sound-recordings.explain: Recordings you made with the Windows Sound Recorder.

def-docs-scanned.title: Scanned documents
def-docs-scanned.explain: Pages you scanned with Windows Fax and Scan.

def-docs-adobe.title: Adobe project files
def-docs-adobe.explain: Auto-saves, presets and project files of Adobe apps such as Premiere Pro and After Effects.

def-docs-rockstar.title: Rockstar Games saves
def-docs-rockstar.explain: Saved games and settings of Rockstar titles such as GTA and Red Dead Redemption.

def-docs-ea.title: Electronic Arts saves
def-docs-ea.explain: Saved games, settings and mods of EA titles such as The Sims.

def-docs-paradox.title: Paradox saves and mods
def-docs-paradox.explain: Saved games, settings and downloaded mods of Paradox games.

def-docs-blackmagic.title: DaVinci Resolve files
def-docs-blackmagic.explain: Project backups, render caches and gallery stills of DaVinci Resolve.

def-pics-screenshots.title: Your screenshots
def-pics-screenshots.explain: Screenshots Windows saved when you pressed Win + PrtScn or used the Snipping Tool.

def-pics-camera-roll.title: Camera roll
def-pics-camera-roll.explain: Photos and videos taken with this PC's camera, or uploaded from your phone by OneDrive.

def-pics-saved-pictures.title: Saved pictures
def-pics-saved-pictures.explain: Pictures you saved from apps such as Photos.

def-vids-captures.title: Game and screen recordings
def-vids-captures.explain: Clips and screenshots recorded with the Xbox Game Bar (Win + G). Recordings are large and easy to forget.

def-vids-screen-recordings.title: Screen recordings
def-vids-screen-recordings.explain: Videos of your screen recorded with the Snipping Tool.

def-appdata-local.title: App data for this PC
def-appdata-local.explain: Data your programs keep for this PC only: caches, logs, downloaded updates and whole programs installed just for you. Usually the largest part of AppData.

def-appdata-roaming.title: App settings
def-appdata-roaming.explain: Settings and profiles your programs keep for your account, such as browser profiles, editor settings and chat history.

def-appdata-locallow.title: Data of restricted apps
def-appdata-locallow.explain: Data of programs that run with fewer rights, such as browser plug-ins. Many games built with Unity keep their saves here.

def-pf-common-files.title: Shared program parts
def-pf-common-files.explain: Libraries and services that several programs share, such as Microsoft Office's and Adobe's.

def-pf-windowsapps.title: Microsoft Store apps
def-pf-windowsapps.explain: The programs installed from the Microsoft Store, including Xbox games. Windows locks this folder; uninstall an app through Settings › Apps.

def-pf-modifiablewindowsapps.title: Store games that allow mods
def-pf-modifiablewindowsapps.explain: Microsoft Store games installed so that mods can change their files.

def-pf-windows-nt.title: Windows accessories
def-pf-windows-nt.explain: Small programs that come with Windows, such as WordPad.

def-pf-windows-mail.title: Windows Mail leftovers
def-pf-windows-mail.explain: Parts of the old Windows Mail program that Windows still ships.

def-pf-windows-media-player.title: Windows Media Player
def-pf-windows-media-player.explain: The classic media player that comes with Windows.

def-pf-windows-photo-viewer.title: Windows Photo Viewer
def-pf-windows-photo-viewer.explain: The classic photo viewer that comes with Windows.

def-pf-internet-explorer.title: Internet Explorer
def-pf-internet-explorer.explain: What is left of Internet Explorer; Edge uses parts of it for its IE mode.

def-pf-reference-assemblies.title: .NET reference libraries
def-pf-reference-assemblies.explain: Library descriptions that developer tools use to build .NET programs.

def-pf-msbuild.title: MSBuild
def-pf-msbuild.explain: Microsoft's build tool, installed with Visual Studio or the .NET SDK.

def-pf-uninstall-information.title: Uninstall information
def-pf-uninstall-information.explain: What some programs need to uninstall themselves cleanly.

def-pf-windowspowershell.title: PowerShell modules
def-pf-windowspowershell.explain: PowerShell modules installed for every user.

def-pf-dotnet.title: .NET
def-pf-dotnet.explain: The modern .NET runtimes and SDKs. Each installed version has its own folder; remove old versions through Settings › Apps.

def-pf-windows-kits.title: Windows SDK
def-pf-windows-kits.explain: Tools and libraries for building Windows programs, installed with Visual Studio.

def-pf-wsl.title: Windows Subsystem for Linux
def-pf-wsl.explain: The program that runs Linux inside Windows. Your Linux files live in a virtual disk elsewhere.

def-pd-microsoft.title: Windows and Microsoft data
def-pd-microsoft.explain: Shared data of Windows and Microsoft programs: the search index, Defender's definitions, the Start menu and Office's installer.

def-pd-packages.title: Shared Store app data
def-pd-packages.explain: Data that Microsoft Store apps share between all users.

def-pd-usoshared.title: Update orchestrator logs
def-pd-usoshared.explain: Logs of the service that plans Windows updates.

def-pd-usoprivate.title: Update orchestrator data
def-pd-usoprivate.explain: Working data of the service that plans Windows updates.

def-pd-regid.title: Software identification tags
def-pd-regid.explain: Small tags that tell inventory tools which software is installed.

def-pd-ssh.title: SSH server settings
def-pd-ssh.explain: Settings and host keys of the OpenSSH server that comes with Windows.

def-pd-chocolatey.title: Chocolatey
def-pd-chocolatey.explain: Programs installed with the Chocolatey package manager, plus its downloaded packages.

def-pd-docker.title: Docker Desktop shared data
def-pd-docker.explain: Settings and data Docker Desktop keeps for all users. The images and containers live in Docker's virtual disk in your own AppData.

def-pd-nvidia.title: NVIDIA shared data
def-pd-nvidia.explain: Logs, downloaded driver installers and shader caches of the NVIDIA software.

def-pd-intel.title: Intel shared data
def-pd-intel.explain: Logs and downloaded installers of Intel's driver and support software.

def-pd-adobe.title: Adobe shared data
def-pd-adobe.explain: Licences, installers and shared resources of the Adobe apps on this PC.

def-pd-epic.title: Epic Games Launcher data
def-pd-epic.explain: The list of installed Epic games and the launcher's shared data.

def-pd-battlenet.title: Battle.net shared data
def-pd-battlenet.explain: The Battle.net updater and the shared data of Blizzard games.

def-pd-ea.title: EA app shared data
def-pd-ea.explain: Licences, install information and logs of the EA app and its games.

def-pd-riot.title: Riot Games shared data
def-pd-riot.explain: Install information of Riot's games, such as League of Legends and Valorant.

def-pd-apple.title: Apple shared data
def-pd-apple.explain: Installers and shared data of Apple software such as iTunes and iCloud.

def-pd-lenovo.title: Lenovo shared data
def-pd-lenovo.explain: Logs, downloaded updates and settings of Lenovo's own software such as Vantage.

def-pd-dell.title: Dell shared data
def-pd-dell.explain: Logs, downloaded updates and settings of Dell's own software.

def-pd-hp.title: HP shared data
def-pd-hp.explain: Logs, downloaded updates and settings of HP's own software.

def-pd-mozilla.title: Firefox shared data
def-pd-mozilla.explain: Update files and shared settings of Firefox.

def-pd-vmware.title: VMware shared data
def-pd-vmware.explain: Settings, logs and network configuration of VMware's virtual machine software.

def-pd-onedrive.title: OneDrive setup data
def-pd-onedrive.explain: Setup and update files of OneDrive for all users.

def-pd-ms-search.title: Windows search index
def-pd-ms-search.explain: The index that makes searching from Start and Explorer fast. It grows with the number of files and mails; Windows can rebuild it from Indexing Options.

def-pd-ms-defender.title: Defender data
def-pd-ms-defender.explain: Virus definitions, scan history and quarantined files of Microsoft Defender.

def-pd-ms-diagnosis.title: Diagnostic data
def-pd-ms-diagnosis.explain: Diagnostic data Windows collects before sending it to Microsoft. Settings › Privacy › Diagnostics lets you delete it.

def-pd-ms-clicktorun.title: Office installer data
def-pd-ms-clicktorun.explain: Working files of the installer that keeps Microsoft Office up to date.

def-pd-ms-visualstudio.title: Visual Studio installer cache
def-pd-ms-visualstudio.explain: Packages the Visual Studio Installer keeps for repairs and updates. Shrink it from the installer, not by hand.

def-local-microsoft.title: Windows and Microsoft app data
def-local-microsoft.explain: Your account's data of Windows itself and of Microsoft programs: Edge, OneDrive, Office, Teams and the Windows caches.

def-local-packages.title: Microsoft Store app data
def-local-packages.explain: One folder per app from the Microsoft Store, with its settings, cache and files. Uninstalling an app removes its folder.

def-local-programs.title: Programs installed just for you
def-local-programs.explain: Programs that were installed for your account only, without admin rights, such as VS Code, Python and Docker Desktop. Uninstall them through Settings › Apps.

def-local-temp.title: Your temporary files

def-roaming-libreoffice.explain: Settings and data of LibreOffice, the office suite: your profile, preferences and history.
