def-roaming-notepadpp.explain: Settings and data of Notepad++, the text editor: your profile, preferences and history. Unsaved tabs are kept in its backup folder.

def-roaming-sublime.title: Sublime Text: settings and profile
def-roaming-sublime.explain: Settings and data of Sublime Text, the text editor: your profile, preferences and history.

def-roaming-npm-global.title: npm: settings and profile
def-roaming-npm-global.explain: Settings and data of npm, the Node.js package manager: your profile, preferences and history. It holds the command-line tools you installed with “npm install -g”.

def-roaming-nvm.title: nvm: settings and profile
def-roaming-nvm.explain: Settings and data of nvm, the Node.js version manager: your profile, preferences and history. Every Node.js version you installed has its own folder here.

def-roaming-python-user.title: Python: settings and profile
def-roaming-python-user.explain: Settings and data of Python, the programming language: your profile, preferences and history. It holds the packages you installed with “pip install --user”.

def-roaming-blender.title: Blender: settings and profile
def-roaming-blender.explain: Settings and data of Blender, the 3D app: your profile, preferences and history. Add-ons and settings are kept per Blender version.

def-roaming-telegram.title: Telegram: settings and profile
def-roaming-telegram.explain: Settings and data of Telegram, the chat app: your profile, preferences and history. Its local cache of photos and videos can be cleared in Telegram's settings under Data and storage.

def-roaming-signal.title: Signal: settings and profile
def-roaming-signal.explain: Settings and data of Signal, the chat app: your profile, preferences and history. Your messages and attachments exist only here and on your phone; there is no cloud copy.

def-roaming-whatsapp-old.title: WhatsApp: settings and profile
def-roaming-whatsapp-old.explain: Settings and data of WhatsApp, the chat app (older desktop version): your profile, preferences and history.

def-roaming-skype.title: Skype: settings and profile
def-roaming-skype.explain: Settings and data of Skype, the calling app: your profile, preferences and history.

def-roaming-zoom.title: Zoom: settings and profile
def-roaming-zoom.explain: Settings and data of Zoom, the video meeting app: your profile, preferences and history. The program itself is installed here too, in “bin”.

def-roaming-filezilla.title: FileZilla: settings and profile
def-roaming-filezilla.explain: Settings and data of FileZilla, the FTP app: your profile, preferences and history. It stores your saved server sign-ins.

def-roaming-winrar.title: WinRAR: settings and profile
def-roaming-winrar.explain: Settings and data of WinRAR, the archive tool: your profile, preferences and history.

def-roaming-audacity.title: Audacity: settings and profile
def-roaming-audacity.explain: Settings and data of Audacity, the audio editor: your profile, preferences and history.

def-roaming-anki.title: Anki: settings and profile
def-roaming-anki.explain: Settings and data of Anki, the flashcard app: your profile, preferences and history. Your decks and their media are here.

def-roaming-godot.title: Godot: settings and profile
def-roaming-godot.explain: Settings and data of Godot, the game engine: your profile, preferences and history.

def-roaming-utorrent.title: µTorrent: settings and profile
def-roaming-utorrent.explain: Settings and data of µTorrent, the torrent app: your profile, preferences and history.

def-locallow-unity.title: Unity: local data
def-locallow-unity.explain: Local data of Unity, the game engine: cache, logs and files that belong to this PC.

def-locallow-java.title: Java: local data
def-locallow-java.explain: Local data of Java, the runtime for Java programs: cache, logs and files that belong to this PC. Mostly the cache of downloaded Java applications.

def-locallow-intel.title: Intel Graphics: local data
def-locallow-intel.explain: Local data of Intel Graphics, Intel's graphics driver and its control panel: cache, logs and files that belong to this PC. Mostly shader caches.

matrix.title: Priority matrix
matrix.waiting: The matrix appears when the scan is done.

facts.steamLeftover: A leftover of an uninstalled Steam game: Steam no longer knows this folder.
facts.steamGameAction: Uninstall it in Steam, so Steam stays consistent.
facts.elevated: Read with admin rights. Unhoard cannot move it, because the app itself has no rights here.

ollama.title: Ollama models
ollama.explain: The size is what removing a model frees: data other models share stays.

docker.title: Docker Desktop
docker.explain: This virtual disk holds all of Docker's images, containers, volumes and build cache. Never delete the file by hand: that resets Docker and everything in it is gone.

errors.notInstalled: Docker Desktop is not installed in its usual folder.
errors.notRunning: Start Docker Desktop first, then try again.
errors.timedOut: Docker did not answer in time.

docker.never: Do you no longer use Docker? Uninstall Docker Desktop through Settings › Apps; the disk goes with it.
docker.buildCache: The build cache is usually the biggest win and only makes the next build slower:
docker.containers: Remove stopped containers of projects you no longer run (their volumes stay):
docker.images: Then remove images no container uses, such as old versions:
docker.volumes: Volumes hold your databases. Remove unused ones only if their projects are gone for good:
docker.compact: The disk file does not shrink by itself. Quit Docker Desktop, run wsl --shutdown, and compact the disk with diskpart as administrator (select vdisk file=…docker_data.vhdx, attach vdisk readonly, compact vdisk, detach vdisk).

errors.notInstalled: That app is not in its usual install folder.
errors.timedOut: The app did not start in time.
errors.failed: Windows could not open the app.

restorePoints.title: Restore points
restorePoints.explain: Windows keeps restore points and shadow copies here, so you can roll back the system. Choose in System Protection how much space they may use, or delete old ones.

storeApps.title: Microsoft Store apps
storeApps.explain: Apps installed from the Microsoft Store. Remove the ones you no longer use in Settings › Apps.

recovery.title: Recovery environment
recovery.explain: What Windows needs to repair or reset your PC. Leave it alone.

defender.title: Windows Defender
defender.explain: Scan history, definition updates and quarantine of Windows' antivirus. Windows manages it; leave it alone.

errorReports.title: Error reports
errorReports.explain: Reports Windows kept after crashes. Disk Cleanup removes them safely (Windows error reports).

otherAccounts.title: Other accounts
otherAccounts.explain: Folders of other accounts on this PC, or of Windows' own service accounts. Only that account, or an administrator, can tidy them.

recycleBin.title: Other Recycle Bins
recycleBin.explain: The Recycle Bin of other accounts or of the system. Each account empties its own.

other.title: Other protected folders
other.explain: Folders apps or Windows protect. Unhoard explains them but never moves them.

suggestions.selectHint: Tick items in any tier and move them in one go; you always see the preview first.

explain.fileOther: “{{name}}” is a file of the type {{ext}}, which Unhoard has no name for; the program that made it knows how to open it.
explain.fileBare: “{{name}}” is a file without an extension, so only the program that made it knows what is inside.
explain.link: “{{name}}” is a link to another folder. It takes no space itself, and Unhoard never follows or moves it.

place.downloads: It is in your Downloads folder, among the things you fetched yourself.
place.documents: It is in your Documents folder.
place.pictures: It is in your Pictures folder.
place.videos: It is in your Videos folder.
place.music: It is in your Music folder.
place.cloud: It is in a folder that syncs with the cloud.
place.appData: It is part of the data programs keep for your account (AppData).
place.appDataOf: It belongs to the data the app “{{owner}}” keeps for your account (AppData).
place.userPrograms: It is among the programs installed for your account only.
place.userProgramsOf: It belongs to the program “{{owner}}”, which is installed for your account only.
place.storeApp: It is part of the data of Microsoft Store apps.
place.storeAppOf: It belongs to the data of the Microsoft Store app “{{owner}}”.
place.temp: It is among your temporary files.
place.programFiles: It is in Program Files, where programs are installed.
place.programFilesOf: It belongs to the program “{{owner}}” in Program Files.
place.programData: It is in ProgramData, where programs keep data for all users.
place.programDataOf: It belongs to the data “{{owner}}” shares between all users of this PC (ProgramData).
place.windows: It is part of Windows itself.
place.profile: It is in your personal folder, outside the standard folders.
place.otherUser: It is in the personal folders of this PC's users.
place.otherUserOf: It is in the personal folder of the user “{{owner}}”.
place.recycleBin: It is in the Recycle Bin.
place.drive: It is not in one of the standard folders of Windows or of your account.

root.appData: “{{name}}” is the data folder of an app or maker with that name: settings, cache and other files it keeps for your account.
root.userPrograms: “{{name}}” is a program installed for your account only. Uninstall it through Settings › Apps, not by deleting this folder.
root.storeApp: “{{name}}” is the data folder of a Microsoft Store app: its settings, cache and files. Uninstalling the app removes it.
root.programFiles: “{{name}}” is the installation folder of a program or maker with that name. Uninstall through Settings › Apps, not by deleting this folder.
root.programData: “{{name}}” holds data that a program or maker with that name shares between all users of this PC.
root.otherUser: “{{name}}” is the personal folder of another user of this PC, or of an account Windows made itself.

video.name: Video
video.about: Videos are among the largest files on a disk.

photo.name: Image
photo.about: A single image is small; thousands of them add up.

rawPhoto.name: Raw photo
rawPhoto.a: a raw photo straight from a camera
rawPhoto.about: A raw photo holds everything the sensor saw and is many times larger than a JPEG of the same shot.

audio.name: Audio
audio.about: Music, a recording or a sound effect.

archive.name: Archive
archive.about: It packs other files together. If you already unpacked it, the same content is on the disk twice.

diskImage.name: Disk image
diskImage.about: A disk image is a complete copy of a disc or drive, often the installer of Windows, Linux or a game.

virtualDisk.name: Virtual disk
virtualDisk.about: It is the whole disk of a virtual machine, WSL or Docker in one file. It grows as you use it and does not shrink by itself.

installer.name: Installer
installer.about: Once the program is installed, the installer itself is rarely needed again.

program.name: Program
program.about: It runs when you open it.

library.name: Library
library.about: Programs load it while they run; it belongs to the program in whose folder it lies.

document.name: Document
document.about: Written in a word processor such as Word.

spreadsheet.name: Spreadsheet
spreadsheet.about: Made in a program such as Excel.

presentation.name: Presentation
presentation.about: Made in a program such as PowerPoint; pictures and video inside make it large.

pdf.name: PDF
pdf.about: A document that looks the same on every device.

ebook.name: E-book
ebook.about: A book for an e-reader or reading app.

text.name: Text file
text.about: Notes or a read-me without formatting.

data.name: Data file
data.about: Structured data that a program or script reads.

database.name: Database
database.about: A program keeps its records in it; the program that owns it needs it to work.

log.name: Log
log.about: A program wrote down what it did. Logs matter only while you are solving a problem.

backup.name: Backup copy
backup.about: A program or a person kept an older version here. Check that the original still exists before you rely on either.

dump.name: Crash dump
dump.a: a memory dump of a crash
dump.about: It holds what was in memory when a program or Windows crashed. Only a developer looking into that crash needs it.

aiModel.name: AI model
aiModel.a: the weights of an AI model
aiModel.about: Model files are measured in gigabytes. The tool that downloaded it can download it again.

gameData.name: Game data
gameData.about: It holds the textures, sound and levels of a game and belongs to that game's installation.

font.name: Font
font.about: A typeface for documents and designs.

mail.name: Mail
mail.about: It holds one message or a whole mailbox. A mailbox file can be the only copy of old mail.

design.name: Design project
design.about: The working file of a creative app, with all its layers or edits.

partial.name: Unfinished download
partial.a: a download that did not finish
partial.about: The browser or app left it behind when the download stopped. It is of no use unless that download can still resume.

temporary.name: Temporary file
temporary.about: A program made it for brief use and should have removed it.

shortcut.name: Shortcut
shortcut.about: It only points to a file, folder or website and takes almost no space.

system.name: System file
system.about: Windows or a device driver uses it.

leftover.goneApp: Probably left behind by “{{name}}”, a program that is no longer on this PC; it last ran on {{date}}.
leftover.unclaimed: No installed program claims this folder, and nothing in it changed for {{days}} days.

history.title: History
history.lead: How full your drive was over time, and what grew. Every scan and the daily measurement add a point.
history.fewPoints: There is not enough history yet. Every scan adds a point, and so does the daily measurement once a day.
history.legend: Point at a dot for its date and numbers. Filled dots are your own scans; open ones are daily measurements.
history.nothingGrew: Nothing grew or shrank by more than 100 MB in this period.

optimise.title: Optimise
optimise.lead: An honest check-up: what Windows measures, where the number comes from and what you can do. No score, and no promises of speed.
optimise.updatesLoading: Asking Windows Update; this can take half a minute…

source.processList: Measured over one second from Windows' process list.
source.storageManagement: As Windows reports it in Settings › Disks.
source.startupApproved: From Windows' startup list, as Task Manager shows it.
source.explainOnly: Unhoard explains this; Windows runs the check.

memory.title: Memory: {{load}}% in use
memory.text: {{available}} of {{total}} is free. Programs have reserved {{commit}} of the {{commitLimit}} Windows can hand out (memory plus page file).
memory.next: Close programs you are not using, or see in Task Manager which ones use the most. Freeing memory with a tool does not help: Windows uses free memory as a cache.

process.title: {{name}}
process.text: Uses {{cpu}}% of the processor and {{memory}} of memory right now.

disk.title: {{name}} ({{media}})
disk.text: Windows reports its health as: {{health}}. Capacity {{size}}, in {{partitions}} partitions.
disk.next: Open Settings › Disks for its wear, temperature and warnings, and back up your files if Windows reports a problem.

startup.title: {{name}}
startup.next: Switch it off if you do not need it right away; you can switch it back on at any time.
startup.missing: Its program file no longer exists, so this entry does nothing. Unhoard never deletes it; Task Manager shows it too.

freeSpace.title: {{free}} free of {{total}}
freeSpace.text: Windows needs room for updates, temporary files and its memory cache.
freeSpace.next: Below 20 GB, big Windows updates can fail. Suggestions shows what you can clean up safely.

updates.title: Windows Update: {{pending}} waiting
updates.text: {{pending}} updates are waiting to install; {{failed}} failed in the last 30 days.
updates.next: Open Windows Update to install them. If an update keeps failing, its error code there tells you why.

systemFiles.title: System files
systemFiles.text: If Windows behaves oddly, it can check and repair its own files. Run these in Terminal (Admin), one after the other: DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth and then sfc /scannow.

pageFile.title: Page file: {{on}}
pageFile.text: The page file lets Windows move memory it rarely uses to the disk.
pageFile.next: The page file is off. Turn it back on (System › About › Advanced system settings › Performance › Virtual memory): without it, programs can crash when memory runs out.

power.title: Power mode: {{mode}}
power.text: Best performance uses more energy, best efficiency is slower. Balanced suits most people.

optimise.startupOn: {{name}} starts again when you sign in.
optimise.startupOff: {{name}} no longer starts when you sign in. Undo puts it back exactly as it was.

startupErrors.needsAdmin: This entry is set for everyone on this PC; switching it needs admin rights. Task Manager › Startup apps can do it.
startupErrors.notFound: This entry is gone; measure again.
startupErrors.failed: Windows did not accept the change.

optimise.previewOn: {{name}} will start again when you sign in.
optimise.previewOff: {{name}} will no longer start when you sign in. The program stays installed and you can still open it yourself.
optimise.previewHow: Unhoard changes only the switch Task Manager uses, writes it in the activity log, and can undo it.
optimise.myths: No registry cleaning, no “freeing” of memory, no switching off services or the page file, no speed promises. Those tricks do not make a PC faster and can break things.

efi.name: EFI system partition
efi.text: Holds the boot loader that starts Windows. Small and needed; leave it alone.

reserved.name: Microsoft reserved partition
reserved.text: Empty space Windows keeps for disk management. It holds no files.

recovery.name: Recovery partition
recovery.text: Holds the Windows Recovery Environment, which repairs or resets Windows when it does not start.

data.name: Data partition
data.text: Holds Windows, your programs and your files.

other.name: Partition
other.text: A partition Windows does not label; another operating system or a tool may use it.

optimise.unknownProcess: Unhoard does not know this program. Its name in Task Manager says more.

chat.title: Ask Lumen
chat.off: The chat is off. It runs on a local AI model through Ollama, on this PC; nothing goes to the internet. Switch it on in Settings.

errors.notRunning: Ollama is not running. Settings shows how to install or start it.
errors.refused: Ollama did not accept the question. Is the model {{model}} installed?
errors.badReply: Ollama's answer could not be read. Try again.
errors.off: The chat is off; switch it on in Settings.

chat.missingModel: The model {{model}} is not installed yet. Download it in Settings with one click.
chat.hello: Ask me about your storage, for example: “Why is my disk full?”, “What grew this week?” or “Which games have I not played in a year?”
chat.privacy: Runs on {{model}} through Ollama on this PC. Lumen sees names and sizes, never file contents.

setup.whatIsOllama: Lumen's chat runs on Ollama: a free program that runs AI models on your own PC. Nothing goes to the internet, and you need no account.
setup.notInstalled: Ollama is not installed on this PC yet.
setup.installSteps: Download Ollama for Windows, run the installer, then come back here and press Check again.
setup.notRunning: Ollama is installed but not running.
setup.machine: This PC has {{ram}} of memory and {{vram}} of graphics memory.

fit.fast: It fits in the graphics card, so answers come quickly.
fit.slow: It runs on the processor, so an answer takes a little while.
fit.tooSmall: This PC has little memory: the chat will be slow and less reliable.

setup.noModel: Ollama runs, but the recommended model is not installed yet.
setup.pullNote: Ollama downloads the model from its library on the internet, only now that you click.
setup.pullFailed: The download did not finish. Check the internet connection and try again.
setup.ready: Ollama runs and the chat is ready.

system.name: System
system.what: The Windows kernel: drivers and core tasks run here. It is always running.

systemIdle.name: System Idle Process
systemIdle.what: Not a program: it shows how much of the processor is doing nothing.

memoryCompression.name: Memory Compression
memoryCompression.what: Windows keeps rarely used memory compressed here, so more fits in memory. High use is normal.

registry.name: Registry
registry.what: Holds the Windows registry in memory, the settings of Windows and your programs.

svchost.name: Service Host
svchost.what: Runs Windows services such as networking, updates and audio. Windows starts many of them; that is normal.

explorer.name: Windows Explorer
explorer.what: The desktop, the taskbar, the Start menu and your folder windows.

dwm.name: Desktop Window Manager
dwm.what: Draws every window and effect on the screen. It uses the graphics card.

csrss.name: Client Server Runtime
csrss.what: A core part of Windows that manages windows and processes. Windows cannot run without it.

lsass.name: Local Security Authority
lsass.what: Checks sign-ins and passwords and guards security policy.

services.name: Services
services.what: Starts and stops the Windows services in the background.

smss.name: Session Manager
smss.what: Sets up your Windows session when the PC starts.

wininit.name: Windows Start-Up
wininit.what: Starts the core Windows services when the PC boots.

winlogon.name: Windows Logon
winlogon.what: Handles signing in and out and the lock screen.

fontdrvhost.name: Font Driver Host
fontdrvhost.what: Draws fonts in a protected process.

sihost.name: Shell Infrastructure Host
sihost.what: Runs parts of the Windows interface such as the Start menu and notifications.

taskhostw.name: Task Host
taskhostw.what: Runs Windows background tasks that live in system files.

runtimeBroker.name: Runtime Broker
runtimeBroker.what: Checks that apps from the Store only use what they have permission for.

searchHost.name: Windows Search
searchHost.what: The search box of the taskbar and the Start menu.

searchIndexer.name: Search Indexer
searchIndexer.what: Builds the index that makes searching files fast. It is busy after many files changed.

shellExperience.name: Windows Shell Experience
shellExperience.what: Draws the clock, the calendar, notifications and quick settings.

textInput.name: Text Input
textInput.what: The on-screen keyboard, emoji panel and input languages.

widgets.name: Widgets
widgets.what: The news and weather panel of the taskbar.

spoolsv.name: Print Spooler
spoolsv.what: Queues print jobs and sends them to the printer.

audiodg.name: Audio Device Graph
audiodg.what: Mixes and processes all sound that Windows plays.

dllhost.name: COM Surrogate
dllhost.what: Runs small helper parts for other programs, for example making thumbnails.

wmiPrvSE.name: WMI Provider Host
wmiPrvSE.what: Lets programs ask Windows about hardware and settings. Busy when a tool queries a lot.

trustedInstaller.name: Windows Modules Installer
trustedInstaller.what: Installs Windows updates and optional features. Busy during and after updates.

wuauclt.name: Windows Update
wuauclt.what: Looks for, downloads and plans Windows updates.

compatTelemetry.name: Compatibility Telemetry
compatTelemetry.what: Collects diagnostic data about program compatibility for Microsoft. Runs now and then.

securityHealth.name: Windows Security
securityHealth.what: The Windows Security app and its icon in the taskbar.

defender.name: Microsoft Defender Antivirus
defender.what: Scans files for malware as they are opened. Busy while many files change, for example during a scan or an install.

smartscreen.name: SmartScreen
smartscreen.what: Checks downloads and apps against a list of known threats.

taskmgr.name: Task Manager
taskmgr.what: Shows running programs and what they use.

phoneLink.name: Phone Link
phoneLink.what: Connects your phone to the PC for messages, calls and photos.

gameBar.name: Xbox Game Bar
gameBar.what: The overlay for recording and chatting while gaming.

msiexec.name: Windows Installer
msiexec.what: Installs, repairs or removes a program.

vmmem.name: Virtual machine memory
vmmem.what: The memory and processor used by a virtual machine: WSL, Docker or Hyper-V.

crossDevice.name: Cross Device Service
crossDevice.what: Shares activity between your PC and your phone.

webview2.name: Edge WebView2
webview2.what: Shows web content inside other apps, such as Teams, Outlook and widgets. Each app starts its own.

chrome.name: Google Chrome
chrome.what: The Chrome browser. It runs one process per tab and extension, so it shows up many times.

edge.name: Microsoft Edge
edge.what: The Edge browser. It runs one process per tab and extension.

firefox.name: Mozilla Firefox
firefox.what: The Firefox browser. It runs several processes for tabs and extensions.

brave.name: Brave
brave.what: The Brave browser. It runs one process per tab and extension.

onedrive.name: OneDrive
onedrive.what: Keeps your OneDrive folder in sync with the cloud. Busy while it uploads or downloads.

dropbox.name: Dropbox
dropbox.what: Keeps your Dropbox folder in sync with the cloud.

googleDrive.name: Google Drive
googleDrive.what: Keeps your Google Drive files in sync with the cloud.

icloud.name: iCloud
icloud.what: Syncs iCloud Drive and iCloud Photos with this PC.

synologyDrive.name: Synology Drive
synologyDrive.what: Syncs folders with a Synology NAS.

officeC2R.name: Microsoft Office Click-to-Run
officeC2R.what: Keeps Microsoft 365 apps up to date and lets them start quickly.

adobeCC.name: Adobe Creative Cloud
adobeCC.what: Manages, updates and syncs Adobe apps in the background.

photoshop.name: Adobe Photoshop
photoshop.what: Photo and image editing. Large images take a lot of memory.

obsidian.name: Obsidian
obsidian.what: A notes app that keeps your notes as files on this PC.

notepad.name: Notepad
notepad.what: The simple text editor of Windows.

claude.name: Claude
claude.what: The Claude desktop app, an AI assistant.

chatgpt.name: ChatGPT
chatgpt.what: The ChatGPT desktop app, an AI assistant.

discord.name: Discord
discord.what: Chat, voice and video for communities and games.

obs.name: OBS Studio
obs.what: Records and streams your screen. Recording uses a lot of processor or graphics power.

itunes.name: Apple Music and devices
itunes.what: Apple's music app and the service that talks to an iPhone or iPad.

photos.name: Microsoft Photos
photos.what: The Windows app for viewing and editing photos.

steam.name: Steam
steam.what: The Steam game store and launcher.

steamHelper.name: Steam web helper
steamHelper.what: Draws Steam's store, library and chat. Steam runs several of them.

epic.name: Epic Games Launcher
epic.what: The Epic game store and launcher.

battleNet.name: Battle.net
battleNet.what: Blizzard's game launcher and its update agent.

riot.name: Riot Client
riot.what: Riot Games' launcher and its anti-cheat service.

xboxApp.name: Xbox
xboxApp.what: The Xbox app and the services that install and run its games.

minecraft.name: Minecraft or a Java program
minecraft.what: Minecraft, or another program written in Java.

nvidia.name: NVIDIA software
nvidia.what: The driver services and app of an NVIDIA graphics card: settings, overlay and updates.

amd.name: AMD software
amd.what: The driver services and app of an AMD graphics card or processor.

intelGraphics.name: Intel software
intelGraphics.what: Driver services of Intel graphics or the Intel chipset.

realtek.name: Realtek Audio
realtek.what: The driver service of the sound card.

lenovoVantage.name: Lenovo Vantage
lenovoVantage.what: Lenovo's tool for updates, warranty and hardware settings.

dellSupport.name: Dell SupportAssist
dellSupport.what: Dell's tool for updates and hardware checks.

hpSupport.name: HP Support Assistant
hpSupport.what: HP's tool for updates and hardware checks.

logitech.name: Logitech software
logitech.what: Settings for a Logitech mouse, keyboard or headset.

corsair.name: Corsair iCUE
corsair.what: Settings and lighting for Corsair devices.

avast.name: Avast or AVG Antivirus
avast.what: An antivirus program that scans files as they are opened.

nordvpn.name: NordVPN
nordvpn.what: A VPN that routes your internet traffic through another server.

vscode.name: Visual Studio Code
vscode.what: A code editor. It runs separate processes for windows, extensions and language tools.

cursor.name: Cursor
cursor.what: A code editor with AI built in.

visualStudio.name: Visual Studio
visualStudio.what: Microsoft's development environment and its build and analysis helpers.

jetbrains.name: JetBrains IDE or Android Studio
jetbrains.what: A development environment. Indexing a project uses a lot of processor and memory.

node.name: Node.js
node.what: Runs JavaScript programs: development servers, build tools, or part of a desktop app.

python.name: Python
python.what: Runs a Python program or script.

java.name: Java
java.what: Runs a program written in Java.

dotnet.name: .NET
dotnet.what: Runs a .NET program or a build.

git.name: Git
git.what: Version control for code, and the Bash shell that comes with it.

docker.name: Docker Desktop
docker.what: Runs containers. Its memory use shows mostly as the virtual machine.

ollama.name: Ollama
ollama.what: Runs AI models on this PC. A loaded model takes several gigabytes of memory or graphics memory.

rust.name: Compiler
rust.what: Builds a program from source code. Building uses all processor cores for a while.

powershell.name: PowerShell
powershell.what: The Windows command shell; a window you opened or a script in the background.

cmd.name: Command Prompt
cmd.what: The classic Windows command line; a window you opened or a script.

sqlServer.name: Database server
sqlServer.what: A database running on this PC, usually for development.

sevenZip.name: Archive tool
sevenZip.what: Packs and unpacks ZIP, 7z and RAR files.

powerToys.name: Microsoft PowerToys
powerToys.what: Extra tools for Windows, such as window layouts and a quick launcher.

googleUpdate.name: Google Updater
googleUpdate.what: Keeps Chrome and other Google programs up to date.

edgeUpdate.name: Microsoft Edge Update
edgeUpdate.what: Keeps Edge and WebView2 up to date.

unhoard.name: Unhoard
unhoard.what: This app. A scan uses the processor for a short while.
